errors.should_be: Classify this as an aircraft-reported/recorded ACARS FM position, not a radar observation. The coordinate pair and 02:10:34 receipt time are correct.
errors.evidence: BEA first interim report, section 1.16.2.2, printed p.45: the last position came from an AOC message carrying the aircraft FM position. Section 1.16.2.4, p.46, gives its payload and receipt time. Final report section 1.9.1, p.49, places the last radar point at SALPU at 01:49.

errors.says: Positions in the last minutes are not published: they are dead-reckoned from recorded heading and groundspeed, fitted to the last ACARS position and the wreckage area.
errors.should_be: BEA publishes a plotted final-flight path; a dense numerical coordinate series was not obtained for this dataset. Describe the displayed positions as a modelled reconstruction and identify the interpolation and heading-to-ground-track assumptions used.
errors.evidence: BEA final report, section 1.1, Figure 1, printed p.23, includes plan and three-dimensional views of the final five minutes. Thus an unqualified claim that last-minute positions are unpublished is misleading. Appendix 2 pp.1 and 9 provides sparse heading/groundspeed values, and p.1 explicitly distinguishes magnetic heading from true track; those quantities are not interchangeable. The plotted path is evidence available for constraining a reconstruction, not a dense numerical coordinate table.

errors.says: EASA’s 2025 guidance explicitly links relief-commander CRM training and experience guidance to AF447 recommendations (s11, pp.3–4).
errors.should_be: Cite s11 pp.4–5, especially p.5 for the explicit AF447 rationale and recommended 3,000-hour experience level.
errors.evidence: EASA Annex VII to ED Decision 2025/002/R, printed/PDF p.4 contains AMC1 ORO.FC.A.201(a)(2)(ii); p.5 contains its AF447 rationale and GM1 experience guidance. Page 3 concerns handover briefing. The substantive claim is supported, but the page range is wrong.
